descriptionFa: بن در کافه با یک جمله خیلی ساده درباره مردم حرف می‌زند و people را در دو جمله آشنا به کار می‌بری.
outcomeFa: زبان‌آموز می‌تواند people را برای اشاره به مردم یا یک گروه از آدم‌ها در جمله ساده به کار ببرد.
scenarioFa: آوا قبل از شلوغی عصر از بن درباره مشتری‌ها می‌پرسد. نقش تو بن است و درباره مردم با واژه people جواب می‌دهی.

targetConstructions.meaningFa: گفتن این که مردم قهوه دوست دارند
گفتن یک کار ساده درباره مردم

curriculum.assessmentBoundary: The Lesson teaches people only as a plural human-group noun. It reuses familiar plural-present verb surfaces and does not introduce a new grammar target.

transferPlan.intent: Understand people in a natural cafe generalization, then transfer the noun from like coffee to the already familiar read books frame.

story.settingFa: کافه، کمی قبل از شلوغ شدن عصر
story.storyBeatFa: آوا درباره شلوغ شدن کافه کنجکاو است. این بار بن با یک جمله ساده درباره مردم و قهوه جواب می‌دهد.

reviewLinks.note: The cafe pair returns after five intervening Lessons with Ben now played by the learner.
The known like coffee frame is reused with people as the new subject noun.
Read books supplies a second familiar verb frame so people is not tied to one sentence only.

languageReference.noNewGrammarReason: This is a lexical-focus Lesson; known simple-present verb frames are reused so people is isolated as the new lexical target.

usageFallbacks.rationale: Do people like coffee? is support language that naturally elicits the lexical target people in a familiar like-coffee frame.
Yes. People like coffee keeps the selected human-group sense of people with previously taught like and coffee.
People read books transfers the same human-group noun to a second previously taught verb+noun frame.
